answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must immediately contact MSHA, without delay and within 15 minutes, after a death of an individual at the mine (or other accidents covered by the regulation).

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, within 15 minutes, once it knows or should know an accident has occurred involving a death.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be maintained with an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device provided to each underground coal miner must be approved and adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: An underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills shall be held at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or designated points of safety.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR 48.5 (which governs training for new underground miners — the course must be "conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions"), each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: This training is conducted to duplicate actual underground conditions, indicating it applies to underground miners.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: Based on the provided regulations, the mine operator must ensure no miner is exposed during a work shift to noise exceeding the "permissible exposure level" (PEL) (30 CFR 62.130(a)). In determining a miner's noise dose used to assess compliance with the PEL, the regulations specify that the calculation must "[u]se a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate" (30 CFR 62.110(b)(2)(iv)) — meaning the permissible exposure level corresponds to a 90 decibel (dBA) criterion over a full 8-hour work shift (TWA8), with every 5 dB increase cutting the allowable exposure time in half. In addition, regardless of the TWA8 average, no miner may ever be exposed to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA at any time (30 CFR 62.130(c)).

claims.quote: Reflect the miner's full work shift

claims.text: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails must be provided and maintained on the banks of roadways where a drop-off exists that is of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment. The required height is at least the mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. (This requirement applies to both surface metal/nonmetal mines under 30 CFR 56.9300 and underground metal/nonmetal mines under 30 CFR 57.9300.)

answers.answer: The breathable air supplied within an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan requirements. The chunks available cover MSHA (Mine Safety and Health Administration) topics such as MSDS contents, control of airborne contaminants, respirable dust control plans, and trade secret chemical disclosure — none of which address bloodborne pathogens.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about OSHA trenching requirements or the depth at which a protective system (such as shoring or a trench box) is required. The chunks instead cover MSHA (30 CFR) regulations on mine slopes/shafts, hoisting buckets, and roll-over protective structures (ROPS), which are unrelated to OSHA construction trench safety standards.
